summary.headline: XtraNet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to ~Rs 51 crore, but EBITDA rose 89% to ~Rs 10 crore (20.59% margin) on services mix.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11% YoY to about Rs 51 crore in Q1 FY27, while operating EBITDA rose 89% to about Rs 10 crore, with margin up 855 bps to 20.59%. PAT was about Rs 6 crore (+77% YoY), a PAT margin of 11.88% (+444 bps). Management attributed the margin expansion to a higher services share, which was about 65-68% of revenue versus about 46% in Q1 FY26. Order book stood at about Rs 373 crore across 55 projects as of June 30, 2026, after fresh orders of about Rs 60 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: Data center infrastructure and IT operations
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 48% of Q1 FY27 revenue; management targets about 50% of revenue long term and 35-40% annual growth in this segment.

segments.name: Enterprise applications
segments.commentary: Contributed about 26% of Q1 FY27 revenue; ERP design, configuration and implementation across finance, HR, procurement and billing modules.

segments.name: Proprietary platforms (Synergy, XtraTrust)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 14% of Q1 FY27 revenue; XtraTrust is a MeitY-approved certifying authority with about 850,000 subscribers onboarded.

segments.name: Digital services
segments.commentary: Contributed about 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue, covering banking support, cloud analytics, AI, IoT and blockchain.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs 500+ crore versus FY26 revenue of about Rs 365 crore, implying about 35-40% growth.
Management expects 55-60% of the current order book to be executed in FY27 (the CFO said 55%).
Medium-term target of 35-40% revenue CAGR over the next three years.
Target long-run mix: data center about 50-55%, enterprise applications about 20-25%, proprietary platforms and digital services about 30%+ of service margin.
Services target of at least 60% of revenue, with a 50-75 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY27.
Effective tax rate of about 25% assumed for the next two years.
capex_capacity: Active bid pipeline of about Rs 1,200 crore; 40-45% is at an advanced stage, and management expects about 30% of the pipeline to convert within the next quarter.
Data center and DR pipeline of more than Rs 600 crore (50-60% of total pipeline), covering DC modernization, new DR setups, NOC and SOC.
Management is expanding data center capacity at XtraTrust to onboard more subscribers, targeted within the next quarter.
Company has built more than 50 data center and command/NOC/SOC setups to date.
Hardware inventory was built ahead of the price rise, so existing government projects are protected from price escalation.
demand_pricing: Government and PSU customers were about 47% of FY26 revenue; in the order book, 45% is government and 55% non-government.
Order book split: about 45% direct and 55% indirect orders.
Around 50% of the order book is recurring (annuity) revenue over 4-5 years; about 40% of the submitted bids are recurring.
Digital trust market: about 11 licensed CAs in India; XtraTrust competes mainly with eMudhra, with 10,000+ channel partners.
Hardware costs have risen about 3-4x over the past year; management reports no cancellations so far, but is monitoring supply.
Product deployment EBITDA margin is about 6-8%, versus about 20-22% for services end-to-end, per the CFO.
Management now applies year-on-year price escalation clauses in new bids, linked to USD variation and OEM supply costs.

qa_highlights.question: What growth trajectory is expected for data center revenue over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 35-40% annual growth in the segment, keeping it at about 50% of revenue, driven by DC modernization, new DR setups, NOC and cyber SOC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance and its drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is Rs 500+ crore versus FY26 Rs 365 crore (about 35% growth), supported by the Rs 375 crore order book (55-60% executable in FY27) and new bids.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete in digital trust and PKI against peers such as eMudhra?
qa_highlights.answer: XtraTrust has about 850,000 subscribers on recurring models, 10,000+ partners, 30-minute issuance, and an in-house PKI engine; eMudhra is the main competitor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle for data center projects?
qa_highlights.answer: End-to-end cycle of 12-15 months; government billing realises in about 120-150 days, and O&M/services billing in 45-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between services and products, and the margin difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Services were about 60% of FY26 revenue, now 65-68% in Q1; product EBITDA margin is about 6-8% versus 20-22% for services.

qa_highlights.question: How do CAPEX and OPEX models and recognition work?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 50-60% of a project is CAPEX billed over 6-18 months; the rest is billed over 4-7 years as O&M. Revenue is recognised on billing with straight-line annuities and no step-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is hardware price inflation passed through to clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a direct pass-through; prices are locked with OEMs per project after order, and price escalation clauses are now used in new bids and repeat orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical bid-to-order conversion timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Government and PSU orders take about 60-90 days from proposal to order; large enterprise, aviation and BFSI take 30-60 days.

risks_watch: Hardware cost increase of about 3-4x; management says product availability is becoming a challenge, and future orders may face pricing pressure.
Margin dilution during CAPEX-heavy phases of large projects (12-14 months), since product margins are lower.
Management's guidance (Rs 500+ crore FY27) implies a sharp step-up from Q1 run-rate (~Rs 51 crore, +11% YoY), and the call did not clarify Q2-Q4 phasing.
Dependence on government and PSU clients (about 45-47% of revenue) with 60-150 day billing cycles affects working capital.
Inconsistent figures in the call: order book cited as Rs 373 crore and Rs 375 crore; the 55% vs 65% executable share and the 40-45% vs 50% recurring share also vary.
Monitor Q2 FY27 conversion of the Rs 1,200 crore pipeline and the data center capacity expansion at XtraTrust.
